title: A short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle in the derived category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category with derived category $D(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and for an object $A$ of $\mathcal C$ write $A[0]$ for the complex with $A$ in degree $0$. For every short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ in $\mathcal C$ there is a morphism $\delta:C[0]\to A[0][1]$ in $D(\mathcal C)$ such that $A[0]\xrightarrow{f}B[0]\xrightarrow{g}C[0]\xrightarrow{\delta}A[0][1]$ is a distinguished triangle.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 0152 (label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor: the delta-functor $K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ sends a short exact sequence of complexes to a distinguished triangle), applied to complexes concentrated in degree 0

mathlib_match.how: exact: for `hS : S.ShortExact` the triangle `hS.singleTriangle` (single complexes in degree 0, third map `hS.singleδ`) is distinguished in `DerivedCategory C`
